transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-20 15:00 PT, Duration ~42 minutes. Attendees listed above.

Summary: quick sync on week-2 of the Private/VPC pilot. Main focus: kernel swap canary results, routing fallback behaviors under egress constraints, and next steps for a controlled cutover. Some noise in the auto-transcribe, names slightly off in places.

Topics: kernel canary, fallback routing, KV cache consistency, quantization profile impact, telemetry gaps, SOC2/KMS question, scheduling dry-run.

[00:00] Maya Chen (Redwood AE): Cool, thanks everyone for joining on a Sunday afternoon — I appreciate it. We'll run through the canary outputs, Diego will walk perf traces, then Nina/Jordan we want your notes on any security windows that matter for rotation.

[00:18] Alex Rios (QuantaMed): Thanks Maya. Quick note — Samir's on mobile but he might chime in for the NetOps bits. We had a couple of anomalous spikes last night around 02:15 PT when a bulk job kicked off.

[00:33] Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE): Yeah I pulled the traces, Alex, I can share a trimmed set. Overall p50/p95 look similar to last week, but p99 had a tail at about +120ms that correlates with network retransmits on your egress path — looks like a combination of MTU black-holing plus TCP retries on the interconnect.

[00:56] Samir Khan (QuantaMed): (voice) that sounds right, we had a router firmware patch queued and one of the ECMP paths was flapping during that window. We patched it but need to validate.

[01:12] Dr. Nina Patel (Head of ML Ops): Do we have an estimated RPS that triggered the tail? I remember the test ramp spiked to 240 RPS for short bursts.

[01:24] Diego Alvarez: Correct — the repro is a burst at 200–260 RPS with long prompts (sequence length ~1024). Also important: when we turned on the higher quantization (8-bit dynamic) the throughput improved but the KV cache warmup produced slightly more variance on the first 30 tokens.

[01:48] Jordan Lee (Security Lead): Just to flag on the quantization and model artifacts — we need to capture fingerprints for reproducibility and to satisfy audit. Is that part of the canary package?

[02:02] Maya Chen: Yes, Diego prepared a canary bundle that includes the model hash, kernel build id, quant profile, and the turn-by-turn perf logs. I'll attach that after the call.

[02:15] Alex Rios: Great. Can you also include the exact runtime flags that were used for batching and KV cache TTLs? Our NetOps wants to replicate in staging.

[02:29] Diego Alvarez: Sure. For this run we used batch window = 8ms, max batch size = 64, kv cache TTL = 10m, prefix caching enabled for common prompts. We also enabled kv prefetch on warm sequences — which may have contributed to the initial p99 blip.

[02:49] (15s silence)

[03:05] Maya Chen: Okay, high level results: canary 2.1.3 swapped kernels in the canary pool — no crashes, error rates stayed flat at ~0.02% but we saw the latency tail as Diego mentioned. Fallbacks triggered twice during the spike — gateway routed traffic to the fallback model variant automatically which kept the overall request success high but increased cost for those minutes.

[03:33] Dr. Nina Patel: When you say fallback model variant, is that a smaller model or same model but different kernel? We need to understand quality delta if we hit fallback in prod.

[03:42] Diego Alvarez: It's the same model weights but a more conservative kernel path without aggressive batched attention optimizations — so quality identical, slight latency penalty. We also have a smaller quantized variant as a last-resort but we didn't need that during this canary.

[03:58] Samir Khan: From NetOps perspective, the router flapping created momentary packet loss, which is what caused the fallback condition to ramp. If we can eliminate the flapping or add preferred nexthops, that should reduce triggers.

[04:12] Alex Rios: Is there a way to make fallback triggers less sensitive? We don't want cost surprises.

[04:19] Diego Alvarez: Yes — two options: raise the SLO threshold for the canary pool, or increase the minimum sample window so transient spikes are ignored. Both are config flags in the routing policy. We recommended adjusting the sample window to 60s instead of the default 15s for this workload.

[04:36] Jordan Lee: Any implication for audit if we relax sample windows? We need to document that change.

[04:44] Maya Chen: We'll put that change in the runbook and tag it in the canary bundle — we include config diffs for any routing policy change.

[04:58] (crosstalk) Maya: Diego — can you talk about the telemetry gap we saw? There was a gap in token-level traces for about 12 minutes.

[05:10] Diego Alvarez: Yeah we lost some token-stream traces due to a sidecar crash in the telemetry agent set. It restarted and reconciled, but the persistence window wasn't long enough and a small slice of traces were dropped. We're adding a write-ahead buffer to the agent in the next build.

[05:28] Alex Rios: That buffer will help. We need full fidelity for the regulatory eval — limited traces make root cause slower.

[05:37] Maya Chen: Understood, we'll prioritize the agent buffer.

[05:45] Dr. Nina Patel: On accuracy — any evidence the quantization profile is shifting outputs in a clinically material way? We ran sample prompts from the eval set and didn't see major deltas but want confirmation.

[05:58] Diego Alvarez: We ran BLEU-like and embedding cosine checks. Quality delta is within noise for our test set — maybe 0.6% drop on long-tail edge cases. We'll attach diffs. That said, we recommend running your sensitive prompts through the eval harness we sent last week.

[06:18] Samir Khan: Quick NetOps ask — can we pin egress for the canary pool to preferred colo? The dynamic routing is great but during the flapping it picked a sad path.

[06:28] Maya Chen: Yes, you can set region preferences and preferred nexthops in the routing policy. We can apply a static preference for the canary during your dry-run.

[06:39] Alex Rios: Perfect.

[06:48] Diego Alvarez: Also wanted to call out kernel-level memory allocator tuning we rolled in 2.1.3. It reduces jitter for 2k+ sequences but requires ephemeral increases in GPU memory during warmup which can increase OOM risk if host fragmentation is high. We saw none in canary, but something to watch on dense multi-tenant nodes.

[07:12] Dr. Nina Patel: Are those memory patterns visible in the telemetry? We need to be sure we can alert preemptively.

[07:18] Diego Alvarez: Yes — we pushed new metrics that expose GPU resident set + allocator churn. We'll publish dashboards.

[07:28] Jordan Lee: On the compliance front, Jordan again — KMS rotates next week for our tenant keys, window is midnight Wed. Does that interfere with your key provisioning for the canary?

[07:40] Maya Chen: Good catch. For Private deployments we rely on your KMS for model key wrapping. If you rotate mid-cutover we need the rotation schedule to be out of maintenance window or we'll need a handoff.

[07:51] Jordan Lee: We'll update that in the SOC2 runbook. I'll send the rotation window and whether there's a forced rotation or staged.

[08:02] Alex Rios: Another small item — latency budget for the app is 250ms p99 under typical traffic; we want to avoid degraded UX during cutover. Any plan to throttle user-facing traffic?

[08:12] Maya Chen: For the dry-run we suggest diverting 5–10% of traffic to the canary and also enabling user-gtg sticky routing so only a subset of sessions see the canary variant. That keeps user impact minimal.

[08:26] (murmur)

[08:35] Diego Alvarez: I recommend also enabling prefix cache TTL reduction for the ramp window — shortens warmup noise. We'll document exact flags in the checklist.

[08:45] Samir Khan: Let's talk about the firmware patch — if we can pre-stage the patch and hold the activation until after the dry-run that'll reduce risk. We can also set BGP preference to avoid the flaky path in the meantime.

[08:57] Maya Chen: Sounds like a plan.

[09:04] (pause)

[09:12] Dr. Nina Patel: Quick question — in the canary logs I saw a few lines mentioning "K-V cash" in transcribe; what's that?

[09:20] Diego Alvarez (laughs): That's the transcription. It's KV cache — key-value cache. Sorry. The logs call it kv-prefetch.

[09:26] (chuckle)

[09:34] Maya Chen: All right, we should capture the specific timeline:
- 2026-12-19 02:15 PT: spike + router flapping -> p99 tail and two fallback events.
- 2026-12-20 05:00 PT: canary 2.1.3 swapped into 10% of canary pool, no crashes.
- telemetry gap: 12 minutes around 04:45 PT due to sidecar restart.

[09:54] Alex Rios: Accurate.

[10:00] Diego Alvarez: For the cutover dry-run we'll propose these concrete mitigations: preferred nexthop, extend sample window to 60s, enable sticky sessions for canary traffic, pre-stage firmware but don't activate, enable write-ahead agent buffer, and pin the canary to a smaller set of nodes to limit blast radius.

[10:22] Jordan Lee: We also want an audit log of every routing policy change — who applied it and when. Can Redwood push those changes through a changelog API?

[10:31] Maya Chen: Yes, every routing policy change in Private is logged; we can provide a signed export and show the audit webhook. Diego will include a sample webhook payload.

[10:42] Alex Rios: Good.

[10:49] (brief side discussion about calendar windows)

[11:05] Maya Chen: Okay last part — timeline and owners. We propose: 1) Redwood sends canary bundle + kernel notes by 2026-12-22. 2) QuantaMed runs the staging mini-canary on 12-23 and posts metrics. 3) Joint dry-run on 12-28. Any objections?

[11:23] Samir Khan: Works for NetOps. We'll also try to keep the router patch in pre-stage until after the dry-run.

[11:32] Dr. Nina Patel: Works for ML Ops contingent on small QA checks.

[11:40] Jordan Lee: I'll get SOC2 rotation details by the 23rd.

[11:47] Maya Chen: Perfect. Anything else before we wrap?

[11:51] (silence)

[11:58] Alex Rios: One last ask — can you drop a short runbook snippet describing how to rollback the kernel swap if we need to? We want the exact CLI/API calls.

[12:09] Diego Alvarez: Absolutely. We'll add an explicit rollback play with the command set and expected timings — usually full rollback within 90s if no other issues.

[12:20] Maya Chen: Great. We'll follow up with the bundle and draft runbook. Thanks everyone, we'll reconvene after the staging run.

[12:30] (call ends)

Notes on transcription: speaker labels are mostly correct, occasional mis-hears (K-V cash etc.). Some timestamps are approximate (every ~15–60s they're inserted).
